headline: Managing Access for the Badlands Multi-Day Trail
reservation: The Maah Daah Hey Trail itself does not require a permit for hiking or biking, but Theodore Roosevelt National Park requires backcountry permits for overnight stays within park units. USFS campgrounds like Magpie and Wannagan operate on a first-come, first-served basis, while private glamping and Medora lodging often sell out months in advance. Always check the official USFS and NPS sites for seasonal road closures and updated trail status.

days.title: Southern Badlands and Medora Gateway

stops.name: Sully Creek State Park
stops.detail: Start at the southern trailhead to experience the rugged clay buttes and initial prairie transitions.

stops.name: Bully Pulpit Area
stops.detail: Observe the dramatic erosion patterns and unique geological strata characteristic of the Little Missouri National Grassland.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for trailhead shuttles; conditions vary significantly with rain.
days.note: Avoid the trail during or immediately after rain as 'gumbo' mud becomes impassable for bikes and hikers.

days.title: Heart of the Grasslands

stops.name: Devil’s Pass
stops.detail: Navigate a narrow, high-elevation ridge offering expansive 360-degree views of the surrounding plateau.

stops.name: Ice Caves
stops.detail: Explore the unique shaded sandstone formations where snow can persist late into the spring season.

days.driving: Mainly walking or cycling; allow a full day for this 15-20 mile segment.
days.note: Natural water sources are unreliable; carry all necessary supplies for the duration of the segment.

days.title: North Unit Vistas

stops.name: Bennett Creek Trailhead
stops.detail: Access the northern reaches where the terrain features steeper draws and denser juniper stands.

stops.name: CCC Campground Overlook
stops.detail: View the winding Little Missouri River from the northern terminus near the National Park boundary.

days.driving: Allow 45-60 minutes for gravel road access to northern trailheads.
days.note: Bison and elk are active in this region; maintain a respectful distance at all times.

intel.title: Gumbo Clay Conditions
intel.text: The bentonite clay surface becomes slick and sticky when wet, potentially damaging bicycle derailleurs. Check the National Weather Service for Medora before committing to remote trail segments.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Medora and Watford City serve as the primary hubs for provisions and fuel. Remote USFS trailheads have no services beyond basic vaulted toilets.

intel.title: Cellular Dead Zones
intel.text: Connectivity is non-existent in the deep draws of the Badlands. Carry a physical map and consider a satellite messenger for the central segments.

intel.title: Summer Heat Safety
intel.text: Midday temperatures regularly exceed 90 degrees with zero shade on the plateaus. Plan strenuous activity for the first four hours of daylight.

intel.title: Trailhead Logistics
intel.text: USFS trailheads like Buffalo Gap have limited space for horse trailers and vehicles. Ensure your vehicle is parked clear of designated emergency turnarounds.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Dickinson (DIK), stock up on specialized supplies in Dickinson or Medora, and verify your trailhead shuttle service.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended for reaching remote trailheads like Magpie; check rental terms for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Scoria Point provides excellent evening light across the red-clinker hills, though shadows deepen quickly in the canyons.
